result.summary: Independently re-ran `mix test test/letflow/definitions/graph_test.exs` on current branch HEAD: '53 tests, 0 failures' (0.4s) -- matches TEST-DESIGNER's claim exactly, real output, not copied from the handoff. Confirmed the pre-fix strictness claim by reading `git show 0f8bd06^:lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex` directly (not by re-running the checkout dance) and diffing it against current graph.ex: pre-fix `check_non_gateway_condition_absence/1`'s guard was `not (exclusive_gateway_source?(...) and edge.is_default != true) and edge.condition != nil` -- unconditionally rejecting every non-gateway-sourced (including HUMAN_TASK) condition, with no CHK-19 equivalent present at all pre-fix; the post-fix guard adds `or human_task_source?(nodes, node_index, edge)` to the permitted-source disjunction and appends a new `check_human_task_fallback_edge/1` (CHK-19) to the dispatch list. This structurally confirms 5 of the 7 new tests (all asserting loosened-CHK-14 or CHK-19 outcomes) must fail pre-fix with the old :unexpected_edge_condition code, exactly as TEST-DESIGNER's quoted pre-fix output shows, and that the 2 unrelated cases (blank-condition single edge, SERVICE_TASK regression guard) correctly still pass pre-fix since neither exercises changed behavior -- the claim holds on inspection, no re-run of the destructive checkout dance was needed to verify it. Acceptance-criterion coverage verified test-by-test against design doc §6/§10/§11: criterion 1 (loosened CHK-14) -> test 1 (single conditioned HUMAN_TASK edge, with fallback, valid:true); criterion 2 (CHK-19 fires) -> test 2 (2 conditioned edges, no fallback, :human_task_no_fallback_edge) and test 6 (single-edge CHK-19 fire, §6 row 1, the flagged no-precedent case); criterion 2's negative space -> test 3 (explicit is_default:true fallback, valid) and test 4 (implicit blank-condition fallback, valid) and test 5 (single blank-condition edge, no CHK-19 fire, the common case); criterion 3 (CHK-14's original guard intact) -> test 7 (SERVICE_TASK source, :unexpected_edge_condition still fires). All 4 design-doc criteria and all 7 named test-spec cases have live, passing coverage -- no gap. Isolation/self-sufficiency: `use ExUnit.Case, async: true` at the file's top (line 13, unchanged), no `setup`/`setup_all` block referenced by or added for this describe block, every one of the 7 tests builds its own graph fixture inline via the file's existing `graph/2`, `node/2`, `cond_edge/5` helpers with only local variables -- no cross-test shared mutable state, no test depends on another having run first. Grepped the block and the spec file for `@tag :skip` and `TODO: implement test`: zero matches in either file. Grepped for hardcoded secrets/connection strings (password|secret|api_key|connection.*string|postgres://|amqp://): zero matches. Describe+test name-length check: isolated the exact block (graph_test.exs:735-845, confirmed by line-range extraction, not the earlier over-eager regex sweep that leaked one line from the next describe block) -- combined describe+test string lengths for the 7 tests range 151-190 chars, comfortably under ExUnit's 255-char hard limit that has broken this file's compilation 4 times before. graph.ex working-tree state: `git diff -- lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex` is empty and `git status --porcelain` shows a clean tree for it -- confirmed unmodified from the committed post-fix state; TEST-DESIGNER's checkout-dance left no stray change. All six of this step's checks pass; no rework needed.
